highlights.text: A Nature paper bookmarked yesterday reports a biomarker-driven combination with better response in EGFR-mutant lung cancer: 76% response versus 61% on the standard regimen, with the benefit concentrating in exon 19 deletion. Fictional highlight; the numbers are invented for the demo.

results.author: Fictional Oncology Review

highlights.text: PD-L1 between 1 and 49% is the gray zone for chemo-immunotherapy: response is real but modest, and the EGFR result usually matters more than the PD-L1 number when both are present. Treat the driver mutation first in the decision order.

results.title: Reading PD-L1 in the Gray Zone

results.author: Fictional Trial Design Weekly

highlights.text: Most targeted-therapy trials require treatment-naive patients, so starting the standard regimen closes the trial door the same week it opens the treatment one. Screen for trial eligibility before the board votes, not after.

results.title: Trial Eligibility Is a Sequencing Problem
